questions.explain: Total storage equals pods times capacity per pod; total QPS equals replicas times QPS per pod. Adding replicas when you've hit a storage limit will not help — Pinecone surfaces that as ResourceExhausted errors on upserts.
options: Replicas increase storage capacity while pods increase query throughput
Both pods and replicas increase storage capacity equally
Replicas increase redundancy and query throughput but not storage; adding pods is the lever for storage capacity
Adding pods increases QPS while adding replicas increases storage
questions.q: A Pinecone index is hitting ResourceExhausted errors on upserts. Which scaling lever actually fixes a storage-capacity limit?

questions.explain: Unlike a SQL WHERE clause, Pinecone's metadata filter is applied after the ANN search narrows the candidate set; the rule of thumb is filters should match at least 10-20% of the index, otherwise increase top_k or use namespaces.
options: Metadata filters direct the ANN graph traversal, exactly like a SQL WHERE clause seeks an index
Metadata filters are applied after the approximate nearest neighbor search narrows the candidate set
Metadata filters are evaluated before the ANN search only on serverless indexes
Metadata filters replace the need for namespaces in multi-tenant designs
questions.q: How does metadata filtering actually behave in Pinecone, and why does it surprise DBAs?

questions.explain: Namespaces are logical partitions created implicitly on first upsert and destroyed when empty; queries scoped to one namespace never see another namespace's vectors, but they share the index's pod capacity.
options: Namespaces are logical partitions enforced at the query layer, created implicitly on first upsert and destroyed when empty
Namespaces provide physically separate storage and independent pod capacity per tenant
Namespaces must be declared in advance with a fixed dimension and metric
Namespaces are deprecated in favor of metadata filtering for tenant isolation
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes Pinecone namespaces?

questions.explain: Pinecone enforces a 40KB metadata limit per vector; the chapter warns against storing full document text in metadata and recommends keeping authoritative text in the primary database with Pinecone IDs as foreign keys.
options: 4KB per vector
40MB per index shared across all vectors
40KB per vector
No limit — metadata storage is unbounded
questions.q: What is Pinecone's metadata storage limit per vector, and what design mistake does it guard against?

questions.explain: The transactional outbox pattern — queuing sync events in SQL Server within the same transaction as the business record change, with a downstream consumer triggering re-embedding — is ranked most reliable; dual writes risk divergence on partial failures and periodic re-index is only timely within batch cycles.
options: Application-layer dual write, because it is synchronous
Periodic full re-index, because it is the most operationally straightforward
Storing the document text in Pinecone metadata so no sync is needed
Transactional outbox with CDC, queuing sync events in the same SQL Server transaction as the business change
questions.q: The chapter ranks three patterns for keeping Pinecone synchronized with SQL Server. Which is the most reliable?
